attribution: Traditionally attributed to Shankara; authorship debated by scholars
summary: A short verse work on knowledge of the Self, using everyday images to show how the Self is distinguished from body and mind.
whyRead: Atma Bodha uses simple analogies, a crystal appearing coloured, the sun behind clouds, to explain Advaita's central ideas in a few dozen verses. It is often studied right after Tattva Bodha.
questions: Why does knowledge, rather than action, liberate?
How does the Self appear to be bound?

keyTeachings.title: Knowledge alone removes ignorance
keyTeachings.text: Just as only light removes darkness, the text argues, only knowledge removes ignorance; action cannot, since it is not opposed to ignorance.

keyTeachings.title: Apparent limitation
keyTeachings.text: The Self appears to take on the qualities of body and mind, as a clear crystal seems coloured by what is placed near it.

keyTeachings.title: The witness
keyTeachings.text: The Self is presented as the witness of the activities of body, senses and mind, itself unaffected by them.

relatedTexts.note: A longer work in the same tradition
